summary: Snohomish Co., WA: 1930 smokehouse-type lookout, reopened 1944, abandoned 1957, burned by 1960; in 2015 only concrete and an old log remained on private camp land.

facts.design: 1930: 10-foot wooden enclosed smokehouse; 1944: lookout with living quarters below and a ten-foot-square glassed room above
facts.status_note: Burned by 1960 per a USGS visit; the register and Firelookout.com say it was gone by 1960. In 2015 some concrete and a single old log remained.

access.note: Private land owned by the Catholic Church and part of a camp that includes Lake Hannan; WillhiteWeb says visitors need permission

events.note: Register and Firelookout.com date the 10-foot wooden enclosed smokehouse to 1930; the 23rd annual report quoted by Forest Lookouts describes the standard lookout type of 1929

Discontinued as a lookout in 1939. Forest Lookouts says the Blue Mountain Lookout took over the view; WillhiteWeb says the Snoqualmie Lookout was built and the area was felt to be covered enough by it and by Blue Mountain.
Reestablished as a lookout point in 1944 per the 37th annual report, quoted by both WillhiteWeb and Forest Lookouts
USGS revisit found a house with a cupola, per WillhiteWeb
A lookout was completed on High Rock during the 1956-58 biennium, per the first DNR biennial report quoted by Forest Lookouts. Does not fit neatly with the 1957 abandonment.
Abandoned by 1957 per the register and Firelookout.com; WillhiteWeb says it was abandoned again in 1957
USGS visit in 1960 reported the lookout house had burned, with remnants on the ground. No fire date given.
Registered April 23, 2012 as US 1246, WA 146; nominated by Ray Kresek
WillhiteWeb visit: some concrete and a single old log with old bolts remained

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Firelookout.com say the site was gone by 1960, but WillhiteWeb reports remnants in 1960 and in 2015. Read together: the lookout structure is gone, while concrete and a log remain on the ground.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: (1) the 1939 handoff. WillhiteWeb says the area was felt to be covered enough by the Snoqualmie Lookout and by Blue Mountain; the 32nd annual report quoted by Forest Lookouts says Blue Mountain took over the view. Story reports both. (2) The 1950s. WillhiteWeb (1952 house with a cupola, abandoned 1957) vs the first DNR biennial report quoted by Forest Lookouts (a lookout completed 1956-58). Story says the accounts do not fit neatly. Neither original report was read directly; both are quoted on the cited pages. Brief height_m 91.4 has no source and is corrected above. Access added as permission. Visit directions from WillhiteWeb are omitted on purpose because the land is private. Not the Gifford Pinchot High Rock Lookout, which is a different site.
